Subject: Evaluation trial: environment needs + proposed timeline

Hi Rishi —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to lock down a short evaluation (2-week trial) to validate throughput and latency for a 3-app integration. Can you confirm the step sequence your team expects in the MAP so we can align our infra folks? Key items for us: org setup (tenant), API key creation & scopes, IP allowlist for outbound from our VPC, and VPC peering/ACLs.

Rough timeline we need: start week of Sep 14, tech preflight Sep 10–11, go-live Sep 15. Security will need a concise checklist and a contact for SOC/peering details.

If you can share a short MAP spreadsheet and the network sample format your infra team needs, we can accelerate approvals.

Thanks —

1) Sep 07: MAP draft shared (milestones + owner fields) — we share 'trial-map-v1.xlsx'
2) Sep 10: Tech preflight (30–45m call) — confirm IP ranges + peering window
3) Sep 11: Org & API keys provisioned (staging tenant) — we generate scoped API keys and share via secure channel
4) Sep 12–14: Network validation (allowlist, basic calls) — small smoke tests

Folks on our side: Neha (onboarding lead) will run the MAP and org/API key flow; Olga (infra) will coordinate the VPC peering plan and sample CSV for your networking team.

I'm attaching the MAP draft and a small network sample for the CIDR format we prefer. Can you confirm your security contact (for legal/peering auth) and whether your infra team prefers a specific peering window (we can do a 1–3 hour window on Sep 11 or Sep 14).

Next step: confirm preflight time on Sep 10 or Sep 11 and the security contact.

Thanks —

Subject: Re: Evaluation trial: environment needs + proposed timeline — technical checklist

On Fri, Sep 5, 2026 at 11:03 AM rishi_malhotra@redwood.com wrote:
> Folks on our side: Neha (onboarding lead) will run the MAP and org/API key flow; Olga (infra) will coordinate the VPC peering plan and sample CSV for your networking team.

Thanks Rishi — quick technical runbook from infra's perspective (compact):

A) Org & tenant setup (estimated 30–60m):
- We create an Aperture Health staging tenant and invite two service accounts (one for integration tests, one for CI).
- Deliverable: tenant-id, admin invite link, recommended RBAC matrix (attached sheet tab).

B) API keys (10–20m after org creation):
- We issue two short-lived API keys with scopes: generate:read, generate:stream, metrics:read.
- Keys delivered via secure link (one-time). Please confirm who will receive (email) or if you need KMS/HSM key wrap.

C) IP allowlist (preflight):
- Please provide the outbound NAT ranges from your VPC in CSV using the sample we sent. Sample requires CIDR, ownership tag, and preferred peering window.
- We recommend allowing the small set of Redwood egress IPs for the trial; if you prefer VPC peering we can skip egress allowlist for private routing.

D) VPC peering (optional, 2–6 hours expected coordination):
- Steps: exchange project/tenant IDs, agree on peering CIDRs, validate routes, schedule maintenance window (1–3h).
- Firewall note: if you have strict egress ACLs, we'll need a small temporary port allowlist for health checks (443 + ephemeral TLS ports).

E) Testing & acceptance:
- Smoke tests: auth, 1k token gen, latencies for 3 payload sizes.
- Acceptance criteria: successful auth + <200ms P50 on 256-token baseline for first 100 calls.

F) Cutover preferences:
- Suggest a peering trial on Sep 11 window 09:00–12:00 PT or fallback Sep 14 13:00–16:00 PT. Confirm which fits your ops schedule.

I attached a condensed checklist in the MAP workbook and included a network-sample.csv showing the exact columns we need. If Aperture requires an executed peering addendum, loop in your security/legal and we can provide our standard template.

--
Olga Petrov
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: network-sample.csv (text/csv)]
